title: Chapter 13. Balarama Dasa, Murari, Yadunatha, Ananta, Ramachandra: Padas from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini* — from Krishna's Resolve to the Prayers
html:
This chapter continues the group of padas known from the *Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed. by Jagadbandhu Bhadra, 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934), excluding padas in nagari-bhava. Here are padas signed by Balarama Dasa, Yadunatha Dasa, Murari, Ananta (Raya Ananta) and Ramachandra, in the order of the GPT sections (that is, of the lilas): the nandi prologue (Krishna's resolve to appear as Gaura), praise of the Gaura-avatara and wonder at the sannyasa, Gaura and Gadadhara, childhood plays, the kirtanas of Navadvipa, the bhava of Radha, the Lord's morning, the people of Nadia in Shantipura, the waiting for His return, praise of Nityananda and Advaita, the books of Jiva Gosvami, and prayers. Checking against the Padakalpataru (PK) showed that nine padas listed as "GPT only" or missing from the catalogue altogether are in PK (nos. 4–7, 9, 15, 19–21) — there the text follows PK with the GPT variants; no. 4 is signed by Vasu Ghosha in PK, no. 5 by "Natavara," no. 8 is Balarama's pada PK 2201 (formerly misidentified with Lochana's pada PK 2203; corrected in the full PK check of chapter 16). Seven padas (nos. 4, 5, 8, 9, 19, 20, 25) were missing from the stage-1 catalogue: they were found in a full check of the signatures of GPT1. Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attribution; padas of several poets are known under the signature "Balarama Dasa"; the "Ramachandra" of nos. 24–25 is, by his own words, a grandson of Vamshivadana who lived after the Lord's departure. The attribution of the padas of this chapter is therefore provisional. The full PK check (chapter 16) found nos. 16 (PK 2512) and 18 (PK 1976) in PK as well; their variants have been added. The Bengali original, the variants of GPT1/GPT2, PK and KGC, and the word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.*

1. Balarama Dasa — "śunaite rāi bacana adharāmṛta…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 2)

Prologue (nandi) of the *Gaura-pada-tarangini: having heard Radha tell of Her dream in which She saw a golden youth, Krishna reveals to Her that He Himself will take that form: three desires — to know what Her prema is like, what its sweetness is, and what happiness She tastes — were not fulfilled in Vraja; taking Her bhava and lustre, making Her prema His guru, He will rise in Nadia.*1

শুনইতে রাই-বচন অধরামৃত বিদগধ রসময় কান ।
আপনাক ভাবে ভাব প্রকাশিতে ধনী অনুমতি ভেল জান ॥

śunaite rāi-bacana adharāmṛta bidagadha rasamaya kāna |
āpanāka bhābe bhāba prakāśite dhanī anumati bhela jāna ||

śunaite — hearing; rāi-bacana — Rai's words; adharāmṛta — nectar of the lips; bidagadha — clever; rasamaya — full of rasa; kāna — Kanu (Krishna); āpanāka bhābe — in His own self; bhāba prakāśite — to reveal the bhava; dhanī — the fair one (Radha); anumati bhela — consent was given; jāna — know

1.1Hearing the nectar of Rai's words, the clever Kanu, full of rasa,
received, know it, the fair one's consent — to reveal Her bhava in His own self.2

সুন্দরি যে কহিলে গৌর-স্বরূপ ।
কোই নাহি জানয়ে কেবল তুয়া প্রেম বিনা মোহে করবি হেন রূপ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

sundari ye kahile gaura-svarūpa |
koi nāhi jānaye kebala tuyā prema binā mohe karabi hena rūpa || dhru ||

sundari — beautiful one; ye kahile — which you spoke of; gaura-svarūpa — the form of Gaura; koi nāhi jānaye — no one knows; kebala tuyā prema binā — except only your prema; mohe karabi — you will make Me; hena rūpa — such a form

1.2"Beautiful one, the form of Gaura you have spoken of
no one knows: only by your prema will you make Me such."

কৈছন তুয়া প্রেমা কৈছন মধুরিমা কৈছন সুখে তুহুঁ ভোর ।
এ তিন বাঞ্ছিত ধন ব্রজে নহিল পূরণ কি কহব না পাইয়া ওর ॥

kaichana tuyā premā kaichana madhurimā kaichana sukhe tuhum̐ bhora |
e tina bāñchita dhana braje nahila pūraṇa ki kahaba nā pāiyā ora ||

kaichana — what; tuyā premā — your prema; madhurimā — sweetness; kaichana sukhe — in what happiness; tuhum̐ bhora — you are absorbed; e tina bāñchita dhana — these three longed-for treasures; braje — in Vraja; nahila pūraṇa — were not fulfilled; ki kahaba — what shall I say; nā pāiyā ora — not finding the end

1.3"What your prema is like, what its sweetness, in what happiness you are absorbed — these three longed-for treasures were not fulfilled in Vraja; what can I say — I have found no end to them.3

ভাবিয়া দেখিনু মনে তোহারি স্বরূপ বিনে এ সুখ আস্বাদ কভু নয় ।
তুয়া ভাব কান্তি ধরি তুয়া প্রেম গুরু করি নদীয়াতে করব উদয় ॥

bhābiyā dekhinu mane tohāri svarūpa bine e sukha āsvāda kabhu naya |
tuyā bhāba kānti dhari tuyā prema guru kari nadīyāte karaba udaya ||

bhābiyā dekhinu mane — pondering I saw in My mind; tohāri svarūpa bine — without your form; e sukha — this joy; āsvāda kabhu naya — is never tasted; tuyā bhāba kānti dhari — taking your bhava and lustre; tuyā prema guru kari — making your prema guru; nadīyāte — in Nadia; karaba udaya — I shall rise

1.4Having pondered, I have understood: except in your very form this joy can never be tasted. Taking your bhava and lustre, making your prema My guru, I shall rise in Nadia.

সাধব মনের সাধা ঘুচাব মনের বাধা জগতে বিলাব প্রেম-ধন ।
বলরাম দাসে কয় প্রভু মোর দয়াময় না ভজিনু মুঞি নরাধম ॥

sādhaba manera sādhā ghucāba manera bādhā jagate bilāba prema-dhana |
balarāma dāse kaya prabhu mora dayāmaya nā bhajinu muñi narādhama ||

sādhaba — I shall fulfil; manera sādhā — the heart's longing; ghucāba — I shall remove; manera bādhā — the heart's obstacle; jagate — in the world; bilāba — I shall distribute; prema-dhana — the treasure of prema; balarāma dāse kaya — Balarama Dasa says; prabhu mora dayāmaya — my Lord is merciful; nā bhajinu — did not worship; muñi narādhama — I, lowest of men

1.5I shall fulfil My heart's longing, remove My heart's obstacle, distribute to the world the treasure of prema." Balarama Dasa says: my Lord is all-merciful — and I, lowest of men, have not served Him.

in.ernet.dli.2015.477854 (PDF p. 261); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 2. The pada is not in the Padakalpataru (PK), the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR), the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC) or the Padamrita-samudra (PS). Padas nos. 2–4 are a dialogue of Krishna and Radha continuing no. 1 (Radha's dream of a golden youth, signed by Jagadananda) and concluded by no. 5 (Vaishnava Dasa). Majumdar considers the GPT unreliable for attribution; padas of several poets are known under the signature "Balarama Dasa," and this pada on the purpose of the Gaura-avatara contains nothing pointing to an eyewitness — the attribution is provisional (C). Gaura-avatara: Krishna, taking Radha's bhava and lustre, tastes His own sweetness (CC Adi 1.5–6; 4). tastes, and the happiness She feels. The poet puts this theological motif into Krishna's mouth almost word for word.

2. Balarama Dasa — "bām̐dhu he śunaite kām̐pai dehā…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 3)

Radha's reply: at this news Her body trembles — He is the life of Vraja; like a fish without water or a serpent without its jewel, Vraja cannot live a moment without Him; will He, leaving Her, reveal prema with His brother and friends on the bank of another river?4

বঁধু হে শুনইতে কাঁপই দেহা ।
তুহুঁ ব্রজ-জীবন তুয়া বিনু কৈছন ব্রজপুর বাঁধব থেহা ॥

bam̐dhu he śunaite kām̐pai dehā |
tuhum̐ braja-jībana tuyā binu kaichana brajapura bām̐dhaba thehā ||

bām̐dhu he — O beloved; śunaite — hearing; kām̐pai dehā — the body trembles; tuhum̐ braja-jībana — You are the life of Vraja; tuyā binu — without You; kaichana — how; brajapura — Vraja; bām̐dhaba thehā — will keep its footing

2.1"Beloved, hearing this my whole body trembles.
You are the life of Vraja: without You how will Vraja keep its footing?

জল বিনু মীন ফণী মণি বিনু তেজয়ে আপন পরাণ ।
তিল আধ তুহারি দরশ বিনু তৈছন ব্রজপুর-গতি তুহুঁ জান ॥

jala binu mīna phaṇī maṇi binu tejaye āpana parāṇa |
tila ādha tuhāri daraśa binu taichana brajapura-gati tuhum̐ jāna ||

jala binu mīna — a fish without water; phaṇī maṇi binu — a serpent without its jewel; tejaye āpana parāṇa — gives up its own life; tila ādha — for half a sesame-seed's time (half a moment); tuhāri daraśa binu — without the sight of You; taichana — just so; brajapura-gati — the fate of Vraja; tuhum̐ jāna — You know

2.2As a fish without water, as a serpent without its jewel gives up its life,
so Vraja without the sight of You for even half a moment — You know what its state will be.

সকল সমাধি কোন সিধি সাধবি পাওবি কোনহি সুখ ।
কিয়ে আন জন তুয়া মরমহি জানব ইথে লাগি বিদরয়ে বুক ॥

sakala samādhi kona sidhi sādhabi pāobi konahi sukha |
kiye āna jana tuyā maramahi jānaba ithe lāgi bidaraye buka ||

sakala samādhi — having finished everything; kona sidhi sādhabi — what perfection will You attain; pāobi — will You gain; konahi sukha — what happiness; kiye — will; āna jana — other people; tuyā maramahi jānaba — know Your heart; ithe lāgi — for this; bidaraye buka — the breast is torn

2.3Having finished everything, what perfection will You attain, what happiness will You find? Will others know Your heart? For this my breast is torn.

বৃন্দাবন-কুঞ্জ নিকুঞ্জহি নিবসসি তুহুঁ বর-নাগর কান ।
অহনিশি তুহারি দরশ বিনু ঝুরব তেজব সবহুঁ পরাণ ॥

bṛndābana-kuñja nikuñjahi nibasasi tuhum̐ bara-nāgara kāna |
ahaniśi tuhāri daraśa binu jhuraba tejaba sabahum̐ parāṇa ||

bṛndābana-kuñje — in the groves of Vrindavana; nikuñjahi — in the bowers; nibasasi — You dwell; tuhum̐ — You; bara-nāgara — best of lovers; kāna — Kanu; ahaniśi — day and night; tuhāri daraśa binu — without the sight of You; jhuraba — will pine; tejaba — will give up; sabahum̐ parāṇa — all their lives

2.4You dwell in the groves and bowers of Vrindavana, You, Kanu, best of lovers;
day and night, without the sight of You, all will pine and give up their lives.

অগ্রজ সঙ্গে রঙ্গে যমুনা-তটে সখা সঞে করবি বিলাস ।
পাসরবি মুঝে কিয়ে প্রেম প্রকাশবি না বুঝয়ে বলরাম দাস ॥

agraja saṅge raṅge yamunā-taṭe sakhā sañe karabi bilāsa |
pāsarabi mujhe kiye prema prakāśabi nā bujhaye balarāma dāsa ||

agraja saṅge — with the elder brother; raṅge — joyfully; yamunā-taṭe — on the Yamuna's bank; sakhā sañe — with friends; karabi bilāsa — You will sport; pāsarabi mujhe — You will forget me (GPT2: parihari — abandoning); kiye — will; prema prakāśabi — You reveal prema; nā bujhaye balarāma dāsa — Balarama Dasa does not understand

2.5With Your elder brother, with Your friends You will sport on the river bank —
and forgetting me You will reveal prema?" Balarama Dasa does not understand.5

me), GPT2 "parihari mujhe" (abandoning me). Radha's anguish is not worldly sorrow but the highest prema (mahabhava) by which Vraja lives; the fear of separation is inseparable from it (CC Madhya 2). the Lord's associates. The "river bank" (yamunātaṭa) is in the poem the bank of the Yamuna; in the Gaura-lila its place is taken by the Ganga of Navadvipa. Radha's fear is answered by Krishna in the next pada: He will not leave Vraja (3.4) — in Bhaktisiddhanta's teaching Navadvipa and Vraja are non-different, and Gaura is Radha and Krishna in one form (CC Adi 4.55–56).

3. Balarama Dasa — "śunaha sundari majhu abhilāṣa…" (GPT1 p. 2, no. 4)

Krishna's reply: He will reveal the prema of Vraja; with all the cowherd men and boys He will sport in Nadia; the two bodies will merge into one, and He will ceaselessly repeat Her name; He will never leave Vraja — without Vraja prema is not attained.6

শুনহ সুন্দরি মঝু অভিলাষ ।
ব্রজপুর-প্রেম করব পরকাশ ॥

śunaha sundari majhu abhilāṣa |
brajapura-prema karaba parakāśa ||

śunaha — hear; sundari — beautiful one; majhu abhilāṣa — My desire; brajapura-prema — the prema of Vraja; karaba parakāśa — I shall reveal

3.1"Hear, beautiful one, My desire:
the prema of Vraja I shall reveal to the world.

গোপ গোপাল সব জন মেলি ।
নদীয়া-নগর পরে করবহুঁ কেলি ॥

gopa gopāla saba jana meli |
nadīyā-nagara pare karabahum̐ keli ||

gopa gopāla — cowherd men and boys; saba jana meli — gathering all; nadīyā-nagara pare — in the town of Nadia; karabahum̐ keli — I shall sport

3.2Gathering all the cowherd men and boys,
in the town of Nadia I shall begin My play.

তনু তনু মেলি হোই এক ঠাম ।
অবিরত বদনে বোলব তব নাম ॥

tanu tanu meli hoi eka ṭhāma |
abirata badane bolaba taba nāma ||

tanu tanu meli — the bodies joining; hoi eka ṭhāma — becoming one; abirata — ceaselessly; badane — with My lips; bolaba — I shall utter; taba nāma — your name

3.3Our bodies, joined, will become one,
and My lips will ceaselessly repeat your name.

ব্রজপুর পরিহরি কবহুঁ না যাব ।
ব্রজ বিনু প্রেম না হোয়ব লাভ ॥

brajapura parihari kabahum̐ nā yāba |
braja binu prema nā hoyaba lābha ||

brajapura parihari — abandoning Vraja; kabahum̐ nā yāba — I shall never go; braja binu — without Vraja; prema nā hoyaba lābha — prema will not be attained

3.4Leaving Vraja, I shall never go away:
without Vraja prema is not attained.

ব্রজপুর-ভাবে পূরব মন-কাম ।
অনুভবি জানল দাস বলরাম ॥

brajapura-bhābe pūraba mana-kāma |
anubhabi jānala dāsa balarāma ||

brajapura-bhābe — with the bhava of Vraja; pūraba — I shall fulfil; mana-kāma — the heart's desire; anubhabi — realizing; jānala — knew; dāsa balarāma — Balarama Dasa

3.5With the bhava of Vraja I shall fulfil My heart's desire" —
this Balarama Dasa has known by realization.7

confirmed by GPT2); GPT2 — sec. 1.1, no. 4.
the Lord in Navadvipa and Puri cries "Radha, Radha!" "The heart's desire" (mana-kāma) is the thirst to taste Radha's love,
not worldly lust.

4. Vasu Ghosha (in GPT1 — Balarama Dasa) — "purabe bāndhila cūṛā ebe keśa-hīna…" (PK 2255; GPT1 p. 18, no. 47)

The Lord's sannyasa as Krishna's transformation: formerly He tied His hair in a top-knot — now His head is shaven; instead of the milk-pail in His left hand — the sannyasi's water-pot; in the Treta-yuga He held the bow, in the Dvapara the flute, in the Kali-yuga He took the staff; Balarama has become an avadhuta, Kanai a sannyasi. Raga gandhara.8

পুরবে বান্ধিল চূড়া এবে কেশ-হীন ।
নটবর-বেশ ছাড়ি পরিলা কৌপীন ॥

purabe bāndhila cūṛā ebe keśa-hīna |
naṭabara-beśa chāṛi parilā kaupīna ||

purabe — formerly; bāndhila cūṛā — tied a top-knot; ebe — now; keśa-hīna — without hair; naṭabara-beśa — the dress of the best of dancers; chāṛi — leaving; parilā kaupīna — put on the kaupina

4.1Formerly He tied His hair in a top-knot — now He is without hair;
leaving the dress of the best of dancers, He has put on the kaupina.

গাবি-দোহন-ভাণ্ড ছিল বাম করে ।
করঙ্গ ধরিলা গোরা সেই অনুসারে ॥

gābi-dohana-bhāṇḍa chila bāma kare |
karaṅga dharilā gorā sei anusāre ||

gābi-dohana-bhāṇḍa — the pail for milking cows; chila bāma kare — was in the left hand; karaṅga — the sannyasi's water-pot; dharilā gorā — Gora took; sei anusāre — after that pattern

4.2A pail for milking the cows was in His left hand —
after that very pattern Gora has taken the sannyasi's water-pot.9

ত্রেতায় ধরিল ধনু দ্বাপরেত বাঁশী ।
কলিযুগে দণ্ড ধরি হইলা সন্ন্যাসী ॥

tretāya dharila dhanu dvāpareta bām̐śī |
kaliyuge daṇḍa dhari hailā sannyāsī ||

tretāya — in the Treta-yuga; dharila dhanu — held the bow; dvāpareta — in the Dvapara; bām̐śī — the flute; kaliyuge — in the Kali-yuga; daṇḍa dhari — taking the staff; hailā sannyāsī — became a sannyasi

4.3In the Treta-yuga He held the bow, in the Dvapara the flute;
in the Kali-yuga, taking the staff, He has become a sannyasi.

বাসুঘোষ কহে শুন নদীয়া-নিবাসী ।
বলরাম অবধৌত কানাই সন্ন্যাসী ॥

bāsughoṣa kahe śuna nadīyā-nibāsī |
balarāma abadhauta kānāi sannyāsī ||

bāsughoṣa kahe — Vasu Ghosha says (GPT1: balarāma kahe — Balarama says); śuna — listen; nadīyā-nibāsī — people of Nadia; balarāma — Balarama; abadhauta — avadhuta; kānāi — Kanai (Krishna); sannyāsī — sannyasi

4.4Vasu Ghosha says: listen, people of Nadia:
Balarama is an avadhuta, Kanai a sannyasi!10

gandhara, MS P-R-Sa no. 2310 — signed by Vasu Ghosha (4.4: "bāsughoṣa kahe…"). GPT1 — p. 18, section "Mangalacharana," no. 47 (gandhara), checked against the scan (PDF p. 277): the same pada, but in 4.4 "balarāma kahe śuna nadīyānibāsī," i.e. signed by Balarama; the compiler of GPT1 himself noted that a manuscript and PK ascribe it to Vasu Ghosha. GPT2 — sec. 1.2, no. 47. The pada was missing from the stage-1 catalogue (new row); the attribution to Vasu Ghosha (per PK) is preferable: the signature "Balaram" in GPT1 probably arose from the second half of 4.4, where Balarama's name refers to Nityananda. marks of Krishna the cowherd beside those of Gaura the sannyasi: the milk-pail in His left hand has "become" the water-pot. (Kanu) is Krishna, appearing as Gauranga. The Lord's sannyasa is not the renunciation of a conditioned soul but a lila for the deliverance of the people of Kali-yuga (CC Adi 17; CB Madhya 26).

5. Balarama Dasa (in PK — "Natavara") — "gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume bañcita…" (PK 2250; GPT1 p. 18, no. 48)

Wonder at the Lord's sannyasa: He whom the maidens of Vraja embraced, whose body was coloured with their kunkuma, is now in saffron cloth, covered with thrills, with streams of tears of prema; the dark-bodied Dancer of Vrindavana has become a pauper begging prema from house to house. Raga dhanashi (in GPT1 — kedara).11

গোপীগণ-কুচ-কুঙ্কুমে বঞ্চিত অরুণ বসন শোভে অঙ্গে ।
কাঞ্চন-নিন্দিত কান্তি কলেবর রাই-পরশ-রস-রঙ্গে ॥

gopīgaṇa-kuca-kuṅkume bañcita aruṇa basana śobhe aṅge |
kāñcana-nindita kānti kalebara rāi-paraśa-rasa-raṅge ||

The pada is not in PK, BR, KGC or PS (catalogue: BD-031). A pada on the writings of Jiva Gosvami (after the Lord's departure) is not Gaura-lila in the narrow sense; a poet who lists Jiva's books lived no earlier than the end of the 16th century (C). Sutramalika, Dhatu-sangraha are well-known works of Jiva; Rasamrita-shesha is his supplement to the Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu; Krishnarchana-dipika is a manual of worship; Krishna- and Radha-pada-chihna describe the marks on the feet; the Sapta-sandarbha is probably the Shat-sandarbha (six sandarbhas) together with the Krama-sandarbha; the Kripambudhi-stava is perhaps one of Jiva's hymns.
